questions.question: At a Prince George store, a 500 mL bottle of orange juice costs $1.50 and a 2 L bottle costs $6.40. Dana will drink all of the juice either way. Which bottle has the lower unit price, and what is that price?
options: The 500 mL bottle, at $3.00 per litre
The 2 L bottle, at $3.20 per litre
The 500 mL bottle, at $1.50 per litre
The 2 L bottle, at $6.40 per litre
questions.explain: Divide price by litres: $1.50 ÷ 0.5 L = $3.00 per litre beats $6.40 ÷ 2 L = $3.20 per litre, so the small bottle wins. The trap is reading the shelf price as the unit price, or assuming the big bottle must be cheaper.

questions.question: Ravi compares two boxes of granola bars at a Victoria store: a box of 8 for $6.00 and a box of 12 for $9.60. He will eat every bar either way. Which box is the better buy?
options: The box of 12, because the bigger box is cheaper
The box of 8, because each bar costs $0.75
Either box, since both are under $1.00 per bar
The box of 12, since the 4 extra bars cost $3.60
questions.explain: Find each unit price: $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 per bar and $9.60 ÷ 12 = $0.80 per bar, so the 8-box is the better buy. The trap is stopping at the $3.60 price difference, or assuming the bigger box always wins.

questions.question: A 4 L jug of milk costs $6.00 at a Nanaimo store. Sam has a coupon for $1.00 off the jug. What is the unit price he actually pays per litre?
options: $5.00, because that is the total he hands over
$1.50 per litre, because $6.00 ÷ 4 = $1.50
$1.25 per litre, because $5.00 ÷ 4 = $1.25
$0.25 per litre, the coupon shared over 4 L
questions.explain: Take the coupon off first, then divide: $6.00 − $1.00 = $5.00, and $5.00 ÷ 4 L = $1.25 per litre. The trap is answering with the $5.00 total or dividing the shelf price and never using the coupon.

questions.question: Priya needs exactly 500 g of rice for one recipe and her family will not use any extra. Her store sells a 500 g bag for $2.00, a 1 kg bag for $3.60, and a 5 kg bag for $16.00. Which is the best buy for what she needs?
options: The 5 kg bag, because the biggest bag is always cheapest
The 5 kg bag, at $3.20 per kilogram, the lowest unit price
The 1 kg bag, because $3.60 per kg beats $4.00 per kg
The 500 g bag, because $2.00 buys exactly what she needs
questions.explain: Best buy means the least money for the amount you actually need, and 500 g costs her $2.00. The trap is chasing the lowest unit price ($3.20 per kg) and paying $16.00 for 4.5 kg of rice nobody will eat.

questions.question: A class needs exactly 30 juice boxes for a field trip. Store A sells packs of 6 for $4.00. Store B sells packs of 10 for $6.90. Which store gives the 30 boxes for less, and what is the total?
options: Store A, $20.00, which is 5 packs of 6
Store B, $20.70 — bigger packs are cheaper
Store A, $4.00, the price of one pack of 6
Store B, $6.90, the price of one pack of 10
questions.explain: Work out the cost of the full 30: 5 packs of 6 is 5 × $4.00 = $20.00, while 3 packs of 10 is 3 × $6.90 = $20.70. The trap is answering with one pack price instead of the total for what the class needs.

questions.question: Leo needs 3 kg of oats. Store A sells 1 kg bags at $4.00 each with a “buy 2, get 1 free” deal. Store B sells one 3 kg bag for $10.50. Which store gives him 3 kg for the least money, and how much does he pay?
options: Store B, $10.50 for the 3 kg bag
Store A, $8.00 for the 3 kg he needs
Store A, $12.00 for three $4.00 bags
Store A, $4.00, the cost of one bag
questions.explain: With buy 2 get 1 free he pays for only 2 bags, so 3 kg costs 2 × $4.00 = $8.00, less than $10.50. The trap is paying for all three bags, or assuming the one big bag has to be the better buy.

questions.question: Aisha needs 2 L of laundry soap. Store A has a 2 L bottle for $12.00 with 25% off today. Store B has a 4 L jug for $16.00 with no discount, and she has no space to store extra soap. Which is the best buy for her 2 L, and what does she pay?
options: Store B, $16.00, since 4 L is the bigger jug
Store A, $12.00, the price before 25% off
Store A, $9.00, which is 25% off $12.00
Store B, $4.00 per litre, the lowest rate
questions.explain: Apply the discount first: 25% of $12.00 is $3.00, so she pays $9.00 for exactly the 2 L she needs. The trap is picking the $4.00 per litre rate and handing over $16.00 for soap she cannot store, or comparing before the discount.

questions.question: A store sells peanut butter in a 375 g jar for $4.50 and a 750 g jar for $8.40. Nadia needs 750 g for a baking club. Which choice costs her the least, and what is that cost?
options: Two 375 g jars, $9.00, as $4.50 is lower
One 375 g jar, $4.50, the lowest price there
The 750 g jar, $11.20 for each kilogram
The 750 g jar, $8.40 for the full 750 g
questions.explain: She needs 750 g, so compare $8.40 for one big jar with 2 × $4.50 = $9.00 for two small ones; the big jar wins. The trap is comparing shelf prices, or answering with the $11.20 per kilogram rate instead of what she pays.

questions.question: Owen's family drinks 2 L of milk a week, and milk left after 7 days must be poured out. His store sells 2 L cartons for $4.60 and 4 L jugs for $8.40, and he has a coupon for $1.00 off one 4 L jug. For one week of milk, which is the best buy?
options: The 2 L carton, $4.60 for the milk they drink
The 4 L jug, $1.85 per litre after the coupon
The 4 L jug with the coupon, $7.40 for the week
The 4 L jug, $8.40, since bigger jugs are cheaper
questions.explain: Only 2 L will be drunk, so compare what he spends on milk the family can use: $4.60 beats $7.40. The trap is that the coupon makes the jug look cheap per litre ($1.85), but 2 L go down the drain.

questions.question: A soccer team needs 24 sports drinks. Store A sells 4-packs for $5.00 with a “buy 2 packs, get 1 free” deal. Store B sells 6-packs for $6.60 with no deal. What is the lowest total cost for the 24 drinks?
options: Store A, $30.00, six packs at $5.00 each
Store A, $20.00, paying for only 4 packs
Store B, $26.40, since 6-packs beat 4-packs
Store B, $1.10, the cost of one drink
questions.explain: 24 drinks is six 4-packs, and with buy 2 get 1 free the team pays for only 4 packs: 4 × $5.00 = $20.00, less than 4 × $6.60 = $26.40. The trap is paying for all six packs or answering with a single drink's price.

questions.question: Ella needs 600 g of trail mix for a hike. Her store sells 200 g bags for $3.00 each and a 1 kg bag for $12.50. She says: “The 1 kg bag is the best buy, because it is the biggest bag.” What is wrong with her thinking?
options: Nothing — the 1 kg bag costs less per gram, so it wins
She forgot that $3.00 per bag is the true unit price
She needs 600 g; three 200 g bags cost only $9.00
Nothing — the 1 kg bag is bigger, so it must be cheaper
questions.explain: The best buy is the least money for the amount needed: 600 g costs $9.00 as three 200 g bags but $12.50 as a 1 kg bag. A lower price per kilogram only helps if you will actually use everything you buy.

questions.question: A Vancouver store sells blueberries in 300 g boxes for $4.50 and in 1.5 kg flats for $18.00. Jo needs 1.5 kg for jam this weekend and the berries stay fresh either way. She also has a coupon for 20% off one 300 g box. Which way of getting 1.5 kg costs the least?
options: The 1.5 kg flat, $12.00 for each kilogram
Five 300 g boxes, $21.60 with the 20% coupon
Five 300 g boxes, $22.50 with no coupon used
The 1.5 kg flat, $18.00 for all 1.5 kg
questions.explain: 1.5 kg needs five 300 g boxes: 5 × $4.50 = $22.50, and 20% off one box saves only $0.90, giving $21.60 — still more than the $18.00 flat. The trap is letting the coupon decide, or answering with the $12.00 per kilogram rate instead of the total.
